claims.text: PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts can catalyze ethanol oxidation.
Conventionally synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solutions have a largely disordered atomic arrangement.
Controlled thermal annealing will increase short-range atomic order in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Controlled thermal annealing will relax local lattice strain in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Annealing can promote ordering and strain relaxation without phase segregation or significant particle coarsening.
Short-range ordering and lattice-strain relaxation shift the surface d-band center of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Local electronic structures of neighboring sites can influence selectivity in complex reactions on high-entropy alloys.
A shifted d-band center will tune the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Optimized intermediate binding will make electron transfer more efficient.
Optimized intermediate binding will alter the ethanol-oxidation reaction pathway and improve selectivity.
Annealed catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than the unannealed baseline.
Annealed catalysts will have lower ethanol-oxidation onset potentials than the unannealed baseline.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit a product distribution indicating improved selectivity relative to the unannealed baseline.
Moderate temperatures of approximately 50–100 °C in aqueous acid or alkaline electrolyte are typical operating conditions for these catalysts.
The proposed mechanism is limited to nanoscale, single-phase PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solutions and may fail after phase separation or significant coarsening.
